blocks.passage:
Calls at work are short and simple. You say hello, say your name, explain the reason, and listen.

On video calls, we also check the camera and microphone before we start. We say "Can you hear me?" or "Can you see my screen?"

When you do not understand, it is okay to ask again. Say "Sorry, could you repeat that, please?" This is polite and very common in English.

items.q: What do you do at the start of a work call?
options: Say hello, say your name, explain the reason, and listen
items.why: "You say hello, say your name, explain the reason, and listen."

items.why: "we also check the camera and microphone before we start."

items.why: "We say 'Can you hear me?' or 'Can you see my screen?'"

items.q: What can you say when you do not understand?
According to the text, asking someone to repeat is…
items.why: "This is polite and very common in English."

audio.text:
Hello, Czarnikow, Emily speaking. … Hi, yes, good morning! … Sorry, I can't hear you very well — the line is not very good. Could you repeat that, please?

… Ah, yes, now I hear you. You're calling about the sugar delivery to São Paulo. Let me help.

… Sorry, one more time — could you say the date again? The line dropped for a second. … The fifteenth. Got it, thank you.

So, to confirm: you want to check the delivery date, and it's the fifteenth. Is that right? … Great.

I'll check with our team and call you back this afternoon. Can I take your number? … Perfect. Thank you for calling, and sorry again about the line. Speak soon. Goodbye!

See — even with a bad line, it's fine. You just stay polite, ask the person to repeat, and confirm the important information at the end.
